# Auth starter

Its files are in [`ext/pages/starters/auth`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/pages/starters/auth). See every [starter kit](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters).

![The auth kit's home page, with Login and Register links](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-auth.jpg)

![The auth kit's sign-in page: anonymous and password sign-in](https://pocketone.dev/docs/screenshots/starter-auth-login.jpg)

Multi-page app (MPA) auth with the built-in `auth` plugin: register, password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 login, logout, email verification (with a resend page), password reset by email, email change with confirmation, and a protected `/account` section (`account/+middleware.ts`). Sessions are a `pb_auth` cookie managed through `ctx.session.*`; the logged-in user is `ctx.auth`. The included migrations point PocketBase's mail at a local maildev and its email templates at this app's `/auth/confirm/{TOKEN}/...` pages.

Templates are `.ets` (EJS whose tags hold TypeScript) and code files (`+config`, `+middleware`, and the `.ts` beside a page or serving an endpoint) are `.ts`; Pages strips the types when it loads them, so there is still no build step.

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp --starter auth
cd myapp
pocketone superuser upsert you@example.com <password> --dir ./pb_data
pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8090.

In another terminal, run a local mail catcher for verification, OTP, password reset and email change emails (the migrations send mail to `localhost:1025`; maildev's web UI is at http://localhost:1080):

```bash
npx maildev
```

Notes:

- Anonymous login needs password login enabled (PocketBase's default).
- OTP login is enabled by the migrations. OAuth2 is enabled with no providers: add one in the dashboard under Collections > users > Options > OAuth2.

## Files

```
pb_migrations/                   the users collection's auth settings and email templates
pb_pages/
  +config.ts                     turns on the auth plugin
  +layout.ets
  auth/login/                    index.ts signs in; _private/ holds one form per method (password, otp, oauth2, ...)
  auth/forgot/                   asks for a password reset email
  auth/confirm/[token]/          the pages the emails link to: verification, password reset, email change
  account/+middleware.ts         sends anyone not signed in to the login page
  account/                       the signed-in user's page, and change-email
```

Live demo: [pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io](https://pocketpages-auth.pockethost.io).
